chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Saffan ibn Yahya, from Al-'Is ibn Al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group of people who embraced Islam in the month of Ramadan, and some days of it had already passed. Is it upon them to make up (fast) the days that passed, or just the day on which they embraced Islam? He said: 'There is no making up (fasting) upon them, nor (do they fast) the day on which they embraced Islam, unless they had embraced Islam before the rising of dawn (Al-Fajr).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting for someone who converts to Islam during Ramadan?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the obligation of fasting begins immediately upon the onset of Islam, contingent upon the time of conversion relative to Fajr. It establishes a practical precedent in Shia jurisprudence where the 'day of conversion' is treated as a full day of obligation only if the individual embraces the faith before the break of dawn, aligning with the principle that duties commence with the first opportunity after acceptance. This hadith is foundational in the chapter of Tahdhib al-Ahkam for determining the precise moment when new Muslims become liable for the remaining days of Ramadan.
